path_builder_foe.description: The path-and-block antagonist: a CatalystFoe that walks and BUILDS — dropping primitive blocks (pyramid/wedge/cube by curriculum stage) to wall the player's route. Befriend it with the catalyst and it stops building and clears the wall it made. Win by outrunning it to the exit, or by changing its mind.
path_builder_foe.name: Path Builder Foe
path_builder_foe.qfep_connection: The wall and the one who builds it are the same problem, solved the same way — you do not break the maze, you befriend its author.

path_game_controller.description: Win/lose controller for the path-and-block game. Wins on reaching the teleporter OR befriending every foe; loses on the watchdog's blocked-path timeout. Pops a pixel thumb over a befriended foe and a pixel heart on a win.
path_game_controller.name: Path Game Controller
path_game_controller.qfep_connection: A game is two truths and a verdict — can you still cross, and did you have to destroy anything to do it; the thumb answers the second.

path_cube.description: Path-and-block game brick: a solid cube wall. Has a collider and is NOT path_passable, so the path watchdog routes around it. The foe's blocking primitive.
path_cube.name: Path Cube (wall)
path_cube.qfep_connection: The watchdog routes around it not because it is heavy but because it never joined the path_passable group: blockedness is a membership status wearing a material costume. Beside the wedge it shares size, shader, and floor — the wall is the rule it carries, nothing else.

path_wedge.description: Path-and-block game brick: a walkable ramp. Tagged path_passable so the path watchdog routes THROUGH it — a cube the player can climb. The gate primitive.
path_wedge.name: Path Wedge (ramp)
path_wedge.qfep_connection: One diagonal face plus enrollment in path_passable turns the same footprint from sentence into gate: the pathfinder routes through, the body climbs. Passability is first declared in a group name and only then enacted in geometry — permission precedes the ramp.

path_pyramid.description: Path-and-block game brick: a 1m-base pyramid mound that BLOCKS the path (you can't cross a peak). Supports the grid wireframe shader. The first primitive in the foe's progression.
path_pyramid.name: Path Pyramid (mound)

path_watchdog.description: Runtime referee for the path-and-block game. BFS-checks every half-second whether a walkable route still exists from the player to the teleporter; draws it as a floor ribbon (green open / red blocked) and restarts the level if the path stays blocked past a grace window.
path_watchdog.name: Path Watchdog
path_watchdog.qfep_connection: A level is solvable until someone proves it isn't — reachability turned from a design-time guarantee into a live, clocked stake.

orb_test_rig.description: Test fixture for the orb gesture slice. Place in a map to bootstrap OrbGestureDetector (under XR rig) and CatalystOrb (under self), and optionally spawn three test creatures around itself. Two-handed forms a sustained dose; one-handed fires a burst with per-hand cooldown. Replaces the catalyst projectile mechanic.
orb_test_rig.name: Orb Gesture Test Rig
orb_test_rig.qfep_connection: Capability-as-relation. The orb is the relation between the palms while the gesture is held; it dissolves when palms part. No inventory item — see /blog/2026-05-11-cognitive-water and doc/ORB_GESTURE_SLICE.md.

pusher_block.description: A red cube that translates back and forth along one axis, physically pushing the player into pits. Uses AnimatableBody3D for proper physics collision. The translation transformation made dangerous.
pusher_block.name: Pusher Block
pusher_block.qfep_connection: Translation as force — the simplest transformation becomes the most direct threat. The block does to the player what the player does to objects.

sweeper_block.description: A blue beam that rotates around a central pivot, sweeping players off edges into pits. Don Quixote's windmill — the world spins and you must time your crossing. Uses AnimatableBody3D.
sweeper_block.name: Sweeper Block
sweeper_block.qfep_connection: Rotation as sweep — the transformation you feel in your inner ear. The windmill doesn't attack you; you attack it, and it wins because it is the world.

grower_block.description: A cube that pulses between tiny and huge, physically pushing the player as it grows. When small you can pass, when large it fills the corridor and squeezes you into the pit. Color shifts from green (safe) to red (danger).
grower_block.name: Grower Block
grower_block.qfep_connection: Scale as pressure — the uncanny transformation that changes everything while appearing to change nothing. You don't move; the world moves into you.

armadillo_droideka.description: Foldable machine-creature enemy with rigid scutes, split equator rings, deployable legs, and fire-bolt burst attacks.
armadillo_droideka.name: Armadillo Droideka
armadillo_droideka.qfep_connection: Locomotion and weapon are one fold: the scutes that make it a wheel hinge open into an armored biped, and the state machine only ever moves between two readings of the same shell. Nothing is added at deployment — the threat was already present in the ball, compressed.

armadillo_eggling.description: Small aggressive roll-form variant focused on contact pressure, tuned for swarm behavior.
armadillo_eggling.name: Armadillo Eggling

dna.default: posture=ball, pursuit=chase - the exact pre-promotion body: the default pair delegates straight to super._process_roll_state(), so the 8 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: zero exports of its own - the base droideka with every weapon switched off in _ready(), hard-coded to roll at the player as a sealed ball and hurt on touch
dna.reads: posture opens the shell without giving it a gun (the deployment was never the weapon); pursuit decides whether the threat is an agent, terrain, or prey

armadillo_eggling.qfep_connection: The base droideka with everything switched off except rolling and touch: zero shots, zero detection radius, contact damage 9. Threat reduced to proximity, and in groups the flanking looks coordinated though no line of code coordinates it.

becoming_catalyst.description: An evolving hand force that grows alongside the player. Not a weapon of destruction but a tool of transformation, becoming, and boundary dissolution. Each Lab sequence unlocks a new expressive mode — from slow cubes to calming fields to swarm intelligence.
becoming_catalyst.name: The Catalyst
becoming_catalyst.qfep_connection: Embodies the full QFEP trajectory: from order (primitives) through entropy (randomness) to the edge of chaos (fractals, L-systems) and collective emergence (swarms). The catalyst IS the curriculum made tangible.

catalyst_pedestal.description: A one-meter wireframe cube display case with the Becoming Catalyst crystal floating and rotating inside. Place this in lab spawn areas. The player walks up, sees the glowing crystal, and grabs it — the cage fades away as the crystal absorbs into their hand.
catalyst_pedestal.name: Catalyst Pedestal
catalyst_pedestal.qfep_connection: The cage frames the invitation. Not protection but presentation — the moment before transformation, when the tool exists waiting to be claimed.

catalyst_prompter_box.name: Catalyst Prompter Box
catalyst_prompter_box.description: The catalyst presented from below: a one-meter floor hatch (one grid cell) whose diamond-plate lid tips open on a gas-strut angle when the player approaches. The crystal rises from the glowing recess; on pickup or walk-away the lid closes, and a timed lease returns the crystal beneath the floor. shape:flat is a flush hatch, shape:plinth a raised box.
catalyst_prompter_box.qfep_connection: The prompter is never seen from the audience — the understage feeds the player their lines. Same invitation as the pedestal, spoken by the floor instead of a cage.

dna.default: emergence=hatch, shape=flat - the rear-hinged deck plate is the shipped closure and flat the shipped body, so CatalystLab_08_PrompterBox (which sets shape explicitly and never sets emergence) renders identically
dna.was: a single rear-hinged lid was the only way the floor could open; the artifact could stage the box but not the floor parting or the vent, even though its own brief (the catalyst emerging from box, floor, vent) names all three
dna.note: emergence is the how-of-arrival axis: hatch = the box lid on its gas strut, doors = the floor parting as stage trap doors, slide = the plate slipping beneath the stage, vent = no lid at all, the crystal rising through a grate in a standing light shaft (kin of catalyst_vent). The fixture pins always_open so every tile shows the offer, not eight identical closed plates.

wedge_skill_pickup.description: A floating orange prism that unlocks the wedge_placer mode on the catalyst bracelet when grabbed. DNA: housing selects how the skill is kept until it is yours (cage = the one-meter wireframe cube, plinth = a solid column offering it, open = no housing at all); after selects what the site does once it is taken (fade = dissolve and free, remain = a dimmed empty housing left standing). Use #housing:plinth#after:remain.

dna.default: housing=cage, after=fade - the cage branch calls the original _build_cage() unchanged and the fade branch still queue_free()s, so all 12 existing placements look and behave exactly as before
dna.was: zero exports and apply_grid_config() was a bare pass: one fixed wireframe cage, as though a cube around a power were a neutral container
dna.note: The cage was an unexamined argument — it says a capability is a specimen you must reach into. plinth says it is conferred, open says nobody thought to fence it. after=remain leaves a scar where the power was taken; it is a time-domain axis and invisible to a still capture.

wedge_skill_pickup.name: Wedge Skill Pickup
wedge_skill_pickup.qfep_connection: The wedge teaches that not everything fits in a box. Slopes, ramps, and angles expand the vocabulary of space.

blockbuilderentity.description: A creature that builds with blocks — constructing and deconstructing grid structures as it moves. The world-shaping hazard that treats the grid as raw material.
blockbuilderentity.name: Block Builder Entity
blockbuilderentity.qfep_connection: It eats the map by the vertex and pays the harvest back as a cage — a hive of blocks raised around the player out of the dissolved room, a thought-label narrating the ledger overhead. Hazard and level design collapse into one loop: the architecture is hostile because the architect is.

dna.default: evidence=result, habit=planar - a deliberate no-op on both axes. result returns exactly ONE figure, the live _current_string, at column 0 with shade 1.0, so the turtle runs with an origin offset of Vector3.ZERO and every colour expression multiplies by 1.0 and evaluates to the literals it evaluated to before. planar holds the roll at exactly 0.0 and the roll is then SKIPPED by an `if roll_rad != 0.0` rather than applied as a zero rotation, so turtle_right is never written and the shipped instruction sequence is reproduced instruction for instruction. The label keeps its shipped single line; the two extra lines are appended only away from the defaults. The 1 existing placement is a bare token with no config, and apply_grid_config assigns only when the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already held, and rebuilds only when something actually changed AND _ready has already built once - so the base's health/speed/damage keys can never redraw the vine.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Eight exports existed and every one was a quantity: two timings, three lengths, one radius, one angle and one damage number. Every knob turned the SIZE or the RATE of one fixed vine; nothing turned the vine into a different vine. The grammar itself, F -> F[+F][-F]F, was a hard-coded _rules dictionary; the turtle only ever rotated about turtle_right.cross(turtle_dir) and turtle_right was never once written, so the vine was a flat drawing; and each generation overwrote the last in _current_string with no record kept. The class had no apply_grid_config of its own, so the base forwarded health and speed and a map token could reach nothing else.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. evidence lifts the derivation this artifact already performs but can only show TEMPORALLY - one generation every iteration_interval seconds - into something a single frame can hold. trace nests the superseded generations inside the finished vine at one root at 35% brightness; longhand stands generation 1..N side by side at one scale, COLUMN_PITCH apart; axiom draws ONE application of the production, the rule as a picture instead of its limit. Generation 0 is never selected by any value: a single bare segment carries no picture. habit lifts the roll the turtle never had - 0 / 30 / 90 / 137.5 degrees applied to the branching plane at each push, planar being the shipped flat drawing and spiral the golden angle. The roll is applied AFTER the pre-roll turtle_right is pushed onto the stack, so popping restores the parent's plane and the roll compounds down the derivation rather than leaking sideways.
dna.kin: evidence and habit are lsystem_tree's two axes, reused character for character, and that is the point rather than an economy. Strip the hazard chassis off this artifact and what is left IS lsystem_tree: the same shape of production rewritten to a fixed depth, the same turtle rotating about one axis only, the same flat plant. The two SHOULD measure alike, and if they do not the harness is lying. lsystem_editor.grammar (koch|sierpinski|dragon|plant|bush|fern|binary_tree) was considered and DECLINED for the same reason lsystem_tree declined it: this artifact's truth statement is `the simplest grammar generates the branching complexity of all plant life`, and swapping its one rule for six others would make it a second editor rather than a vine. branching_coral.growth_form was declined on the same ground - it is a grammar axis under another name.
dna.declined: TROPISM - which way the growth leans - was the obvious axis to reach for, because it is what this artifact alone among the L-system family argues: its @identity says `the vine does not chase, it grows toward you`, and player_bias = 0.3 is a real hard-coded constant that bends every segment. It was declined because it CANNOT BE PHOTOGRAPHED. _walk reads the bias only inside `if is_instance_valid(_player_node)`, and there is no player on the bench, so bias_dir stays Vector3.ZERO and biased_dir falls back to turtle_dir. A `hunt` value and a `plumb` value would therefore render the same vine to the byte - two rungs at 0.00% - which is precisely the finished-looking experiment that answers nothing. The hunting is real, it is simply invisible to a still with nothing to hunt. Pruning was declined for the same reason: _on_damaged is the vine's other distinctive mechanic and nothing damages it on a bench.
dna.fixture_note: all three are quantities at their shipped values in every real room, so they are bench knobs and not axes. iteration_interval is the one that MATTERS: the shipped 3.0 s with max_iterations 4 means the vine needs twelve seconds to finish growing, and a capture that lands four or five seconds in photographs it at generation 1 - where `result` and `axiom` are the same string and would render two identical frames. At 0.05 s the derivation is complete in a fifth of a second and all four evidence rungs are distinct. patrol_speed 0 and detection_radius 0 pin the creature: this is a CharacterBody3D that walks its patrol corners from the first physics frame, and an unpinned creature drifts inside a fixed sweep camera so the diff measures displacement instead of the axis. Both only bite because _on_ready's writes were changed to fire only while the property still holds HazardCreatureBase's default - an unguarded write there discards anything set before add_child, which is exactly how the sweep applies values.
dna.still_note: every rung of both axes is standing geometry - a set of cylinders and leaf spheres that exists as soon as the turtle has walked. The gentle sway in _process_visual is phase-locked to _walk_phase, which starts at 0 in every variant and only advances in PATROL or CHASE, so read the sway as shared noise across all frames rather than as signal.
dna.reads: the .tscn root is the scripted node (CharacterBody3D carrying branching_vine.gd, class_name BranchingVine) so both axes are reachable from a map token and from the sweep.

branching_vine.description: L-system vine growing from a root point. Turtle graphics interpretation builds cylinder branches that reach toward the player. Damage prunes random branches. Formal grammar becomes organic growth.
branching_vine.name: Branching Vine
branching_vine.qfep_connection: One rewrite rule — F becomes F[+F][-F]F — plus a bias term leaning each branch toward your position: it does not chase, it compiles toward you every three seconds. Pruning is the only counterargument the grammar understands.

dna.default: salvage=mixed, assembly=figure - mixed is the shipped randi_range(0, 3) draw over box/sphere/cylinder/prism and figure returns the six SLOT_POSITIONS literals unchanged, so the 1 existing placement builds the same golem it always did; part_seed=0 keeps the unseeded global RNG, which is what shipped
dna.was: five exports and every one of them a duration or a multiplier - rebuild_time, rebuild_heal_pct, max_rebuilds, part_scatter_distance, exhausted_speed_mult. Nothing a still can see. The two decisions carrying the bricolage argument were literals in the body of _random_mesh() and a const array of six humanoid slot positions
dna.reads: salvage is WHAT IS AT HAND: a heterogeneous junk pile makes the improvisation visible, and each single-stock pile (crates, pipes, stones, offcuts) hands the bricoleur a warehouse instead, so the golem comes out looking designed. assembly is WHAT IS DONE WITH IT: figure forces found parts into a body plan they never had, lashed lets the joints show, cairn abandons anatomy for stacking, heap refuses to stand the parts up at all
dna.fixture_note: the shipped golem draws from the global RNG, so five unseeded variants are five different golems and any measured bite is noise. part_seed pins the stream for the gallery only; the default 0 is still the shipped behaviour
dna.declined: a colour axis. The six random hues are the same argument salvage already makes, one register down, and it would have cost a second knob to say it twice

bricoleur_golem.description: Asymmetric golem built from mismatched primitives. Rebuilds itself from random parts after damage — each reconstruction unique. Exhausts after 3 rebuilds. Teaches bricolage: creation from whatever is at hand.
bricoleur_golem.name: Bricoleur Golem
bricoleur_golem.qfep_connection: Damage is a commission: each hit scatters the six body slots and the rebuild draws new random primitives into them, never the same golem twice. The exhaustion counter admits what bricolage costs — three reinventions and the improvising body runs out of flux.

dna.default: rig=free + mark=none returns before allocating anything; 100 placements unchanged.
dna.note: APPEARANCE ONLY - collision, damage, timing and triggers are untouched, because existing maps depend on this artifact's hazard behaviour. RENAMED from `mount` to `rig` after the review: exhibit_furniture#mount:<lookup_name> already means the artifact seated ON that bed across 500+ placements, and this meant the rig holding the target - two opposite senses of one token is a trap for whoever writes the next map.

catalyst_target.description: A practice target that flashes, explodes, and respawns when struck. Its visible states change quickly, but the target remains recognizably the same object across idle, hit, destroyed, and restored phases. Movement options add patrol and orbit patterns without changing that core identity. It is a compact lesson in state transition.
catalyst_target.name: Catalyst Target
catalyst_target.qfep_connection: Transformation here is discrete state change: intact, flashing, destroyed, respawned. Identity persists while S moves through a small cycle of visibly distinct modes.
catalyst_target.capacity: TRACK a target through hit, destroy, and respawn states while keeping its identity legible.
interactions: hit the target with catalyst projectiles
switch between static, patrolling, and orbiting motion via config
change the target shape to compare different visual states
watch the respawn loop reset the object after destruction

chromatic_field.description: RGB zone hazard with three overlapping translucent spheres cycling through hue. Damage type depends on the dominant color channel — red heat, green poison, blue cold. Teaches color mixing and perception.
chromatic_field.name: Chromatic Field
chromatic_field.qfep_connection: Hue is repurposed as a damage taxonomy — whichever channel dominates the cycling phase decides whether you burn, poison, or freeze. Color stops being appearance and becomes protocol; reading the spectrum correctly is the only armor on offer.

collision_crasher.description: Central body with 5 tethered physics blocks that bounce and collide with elastic collision math. Impulse vectors visible as arrows on impact. Momentum conservation made tangible.
collision_crasher.name: Collision Crasher

dna.default: tether=none - a deliberate no-op. _build_tether() returns on its first line before constructing anything, so the scene tree, the capture AABB and every material are byte-identical to the pre-promotion build, and _process_visual's new branch is skipped by a string compare. block_seed 0 is the shipped unseeded global RNG: _block_randf falls straight through to the same randf_range calls, in the same order, with the same three draws per block. apply_grid_config now OVERRIDES the base class's, and the first thing it does is `super.apply_grid_config(config)`, so the existing health / speed / chase_speed / damage / detection_radius keys keep working exactly as before; the two new keys are guarded twice, and _rebuild() fires only after _build_mesh has run once. The placements pass no tether key - the direct grid token in Hazards_Zoo_5, and the curation_station rosters in VFM_03_Motion, Trial_eye_VFM_03_Motion, Curation_Bay_hazards_3 and Corridor_VFM_03_Motion - so none of them reaches an assignment and none of them rebuilds.
dna.was: seven @export knobs and not one categorical among them: a count, two lengths, a spring constant, a damping rate and two damage numbers. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.finding: THE TETHER WAS NEVER DRAWN. The class is named CollisionCrasher, its own doc says '5 tethered BoxMesh blocks', its @identity names 'tether length' as its critical parameter and the registry description says 'tethered physics blocks' - and there has never been a tether in the scene. The constraint is a spring force computed in _process_visual against tether_radius and depicted by nothing, so what a player meets is five cubes hovering near a sphere for no visible reason. SECOND: the impulse arrows, which the description and the @identity both present as this artifact's evidence ('Impulse vectors visible as arrows on impact'), only spawn when a block comes within 0.3 m of the PLAYER. Nobody has ever seen them in a still and most players will not have seen them at all. They are left as they are - firing them without a player would change what five rooms draw - but they are not the evidence this entry claims.
dna.kin: tether is a NEW word and two existing ones were considered and refused. `warning` (none | stain | cage | beacon | shroud, force_vortex and nine siblings) is the hazard family's word and this IS a hazard, but warning asks how legible the DANGER is to a player and two of its five values - stain and beacon - would have to be answered with something this object does not do. A boundary drawn here is not a threat announcement; it is a physics constraint, and the danger is the blocks, not the sphere they are held inside. `disclosure` (bias_visualizer, penrose_triangle, cube_lines) fits the shape of the question - how much of its own working the object shows - but each of its siblings carries a bespoke value list, so the shared word would carry nothing across. Taking a word without its answers is the folding_past fault, so both were left where they are.
dna.note: tether is an ORDINAL ladder of how much of the constraint is drawn: nothing, the individual links, the boundary implied, the boundary made solid. Every value leaves the physics untouched - the same spring, the same tether_radius, the same perfectly elastic block-block impulse - so the axis is strictly about depiction. line is the one that says something the others cannot: it shows each block held to the CENTRE and not to its neighbours, which is exactly the claim the code makes and the picture denies.
dna.still_note: READ BEFORE CALLING A RUNG INERT. shell and cage are the strong values: a 0.8 m sphere or three 0.8 m rings against a subject whose largest existing mesh is a 0.24 m body, in a frame that dna.framing pins at roughly 2.3 m. line is the THIN rung by construction - five rods of 6 mm radius and at most 0.4 m length, on the order of 1% of frame - so crop-recheck it before believing an INERT verdict; it is thin because a tether is thin, not because the value does nothing. dna.framing is 0.75 because at 1.0 the fit-to-AABB shot is about 3 m wide for roughly 1% lit pixels; 0.75 is deliberately not tighter because THE BODIES MOVE BETWEEN THE PRE-PASS AND THE SHUTTER - the union AABB is measured at 0.35 s and the frame is written at 1.1 s, the fault newtons_laws documented - so the margin is there to stop the axis cropping the very blocks it is about.
dna.declines: num_blocks, block_size, tether_radius, tether_k, block_damping, chase_tether_bonus and block_damage stay plain exports: five are magnitudes and two are rates. `regime` (bouncing_ball's restitution word) was refused with a reason - see the header block in collision_crasher.gd: restitution is a rate of energy loss and a still catches one arbitrary instant of a chaotic five-body bounce, and the static envelope bouncing_ball drew instead is, here, precisely what `tether` already draws. `configuration` (three_body_problem, nbody_simulation) was refused too: nbody qualifies because its bodies drift ~0.002 per frame against a 0.35 m radius so t=0 survives the settle, while a block here starts at 0.5-1.5 m/s inside a 0.4 m tether and has crossed its cage many times before the shutter falls.

collision_crasher.qfep_connection: F_force: momentum conservation made tangible — five tethered blocks colliding elastically around a central body, impulse arrows at every impact. What is exchanged is never lost, only redirected.

constraint_web.description: 5x5 grid of superposition tiles representing a constraint satisfaction problem. Tiles collapse on step; contradictions explode. Graph coloring as minefield — no two adjacent tiles may share a color.
constraint_web.name: Constraint Web
constraint_web.qfep_connection: Every tile flickers through the colors it might still be until your footfall collapses it, and the no-two-adjacent constraint propagates outward from where you stood. An emptied domain detonates — contradiction made a physical event, billed to whoever committed first.

data_tree_walker.description: Binary search tree of sphere nodes connected by cylinder edges. BST insert with values 1-7; visible tree rotations on damage. Walks on its leaf nodes. Data structures made physical.
data_tree_walker.name: Data Tree Walker
data_tree_walker.qfep_connection: Seven values in a balanced BST, and the abstraction is made to carry weight — it stands on its own leaf nodes. Damage triggers visible rotations: the structure defends its O(log n) the way a body defends its posture.

deltahedron_creature.description: A creature whose body IS its mesh net. Flat at fold_amount=0, assembled convex solid at fold_amount=1. All equilateral triangles — Cauchy's rigidity theorem guarantees structural integrity when closed. Species: tetrahedron (4), octahedron (8), icosahedron (20).
deltahedron_creature.name: Deltahedron Creature
deltahedron_creature.qfep_connection: Cauchy's rigidity theorem does the character design: closed, convex, all-triangle, the finished body cannot flex — so vulnerability lives entirely below fold_amount 1, in the unfolding. Species differ only in net topology; the genome is a crease pattern.

deltahedron_stages.description: Five octahedra in a row at fold_amount 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. Shows the complete net-to-solid fold progression in one glance. Blue (flat) to gold (assembled).
deltahedron_stages.name: Deltahedron Stages
deltahedron_stages.qfep_connection: One fold variable sampled five times and laid in a row: the octahedron's whole becoming, flat net to rigid solid, spatialized so the eye can walk the derivative. Time traded for distance — a transformation rendered as still life.

edible_mushroom.description: Pickable mushroom with transformative effects. RAND Corporation 1955 meets fungal spores — historical randomness made edible. Consume to trigger perceptual shifts.
edible_mushroom.name: Edible Mushroom
edible_mushroom.qfep_connection: Eating is implemented as proximity — hold it within 0.25 m of the camera and consumption fires, the mouth inferred from the head. Swallowing, the one gesture VR cannot give you, is skipped straight to its consequence: a shader rewrites perception and the form that caused it dissolves.

escher_stairwalker.description: Minimalist figure walking an impossible staircase loop. Always appears to climb but stays at the same height. Invulnerable while on stairs; glitches out to lunge. Impossible geometry as armor.
escher_stairwalker.name: Escher Stairwalker
escher_stairwalker.qfep_connection: Every step is locally valid; the loop sums to zero height — and inside that contradiction it cannot be hurt. It becomes vulnerable only when it glitches off the stairs to lunge: touching shared space is the price of leaving the representation.

fallingblocks.description: Environmental hazard that spawns falling block formations. Gravity as threat — the grid raining down. Dodge, shelter, or ride the cascade.
fallingblocks.name: Falling Blocks
fallingblocks.qfep_connection: A timer hands one cube at a time to gravity, and a hit costs position rather than flesh — you are posted back to spawn. Danger reduced to a schedule: no aim, no chase, just physics keeping an appointment above your head.

fibonacci_snake.description: Triangle strip coiled in a golden spiral unfolds into a slithering sine-wave snake. Phi encodes rest, sin encodes motion. Same vertices, same faces — only positions change.
fibonacci_snake.name: Fibonacci Snake
fibonacci_snake.qfep_connection: Rest is a golden spiral, motion a phase-shifted sine, and fold_amount is the only word the body has for the difference. No vertex is added or removed between coil and slither — identity survives as topology while every position defects.

fibonacci_snake_stages.description: Five stages: Fibonacci spiral to sine snake. Golden ratio coil unfurling into wave locomotion. Same vertex and face count throughout.
fibonacci_snake_stages.name: Fibonacci Snake Stages
fibonacci_snake_stages.qfep_connection: Phi-spiral and sine snake share every vertex and every face; the five stages merely lerp coordinates between the two poses. Two apparent species collapse into one topology — morphology exposed as a slider position, not an essence.

five_leg_critter.description: Five-legged procedural walker. Odd symmetry forces asymmetric gait patterns — starfish-like radial locomotion.
five_leg_critter.name: Five Leg Critter
five_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Placed at 72°, no foot has a mirror partner, so the step rule cannot relax into any inherited gait — every stride is improvised against the stretch threshold, one leg at a time. Five is the prime that keeps locomotion honest: walking with no symmetry to lean on.

flora_landscape.description: Renders the Folding Zoo nature_layer.json as a 3D landscape. Vertex-colored ground mesh with MultiMesh flora on top.
flora_landscape.name: Flora Landscape
flora_landscape.qfep_connection: A JSON layer file stands up as terrain: ground types become vertex colors, flora entries become MultiMesh instances, the rng seed pinned at 12345. Landscape as a saved document — the same nature every load, which is exactly what a document promises and a landscape never does.

fold_demo_critter.description: Four-segment folding creature — wings spread open and tail lifts as fold_amount increases. Demonstrates BoneFoldSolver with spring dynamics, energy gating, and misfold. The simplest possible folding body.
fold_demo_critter.name: Fold Demo Critter
fold_demo_critter.qfep_connection: Four segments, one spring solver, and a state machine that only spreads the wings when the world reads as safe — the tail lift waits behind wing progress. The gating is the point: unfolding as trust made mechanical.

fold_wall.description: Triangulated curtain pooled flat on the ground rises into a hanging drape. Columns cascade left to right with sine billow for fabric feel. Same vertices, same faces.
fold_wall.name: Fold Wall / Curtain
fold_wall.qfep_connection: A floor's worth of triangles hinges up into a curtain, columns cascading left to right with a sine billow laid over the rigid grid. The vertices that lay pooled now hang from the same faces — verticality as a remembered posture, not new geometry.

folding_zoo.description: Six-zone interactive showcase of the fold system — bone fold, chain fold, shell fold, state parade, misfold, and spring tension. All three solvers demonstrated with debug overlays.
folding_zoo.name: Folding Zoo
folding_zoo.qfep_connection: Six enclosures, three solvers, one sinusoidal _global_fold breathing through everything — comparative anatomy where specimens differ only in how they interpret the same scalar. That misfold gets its own zone matters: failure is admitted as a fold family, not an exception.

foliage_showcase.description: All 8 synthetic plant types side by side — grass, flower, fern, mushroom, reed, tree, bush, vine. Low-poly procedural meshes for MultiMesh instancing.
foliage_showcase.name: Foliage Showcase
foliage_showcase.qfep_connection: Eight plants in a police lineup, each a low-poly mesh built for MultiMesh multiplication — the botany here is logistics, nature pre-formatted for instancing. Before a forest can exist in this world, each species must first become a part number.

force_field.description: Dual-nature force zone: every hazard is also medicine. Fire warms or burns. Poison kills or reveals. Q-FEP: same potential, different restraint, different manifestation. Bring a mediator object into the field to transmute hazard into benefit.
force_field.name: Force Field
force_field.qfep_connection: Central demonstration of Q-FEP: identical potential under different relational constraint produces opposite outcomes. The player experiences this directly.

four_leg_critter.description: Four-legged procedural walker. Quadruped gait with diagonal pairing — walk, trot, gallop emerge from phase relationships between legs.
four_leg_critter.name: Four Leg Critter
four_leg_critter.qfep_connection: The feet sit at the four corners and none is told about the others: each simply steps when the body's drift stretches it past its threshold. Whatever reads as a trot is a settlement among four independent deadlines — the vertebrate gait recovered as emergence, not choreography.

dna.default: start_depth=0 - the crown builder at depth 0 emits exactly the two calls _on_ready() used to make by hand, angles -0.5 then 0.5, base_head_size, depth 0, in that order, so the head materials land in the same slots too. The 1 existing placement passes no start_depth, and apply_grid_config regrows only when the value both parses and differs, so that room is unchanged.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Six exports existed and all six were quantities: a ceiling, three lengths, a speed and a damage number. The decision that carries the argument, how far the branching has already gone, was a pair of literal _add_head calls in _on_ready.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. max_depth WAS already an export and is deliberately still not declared: it is a ceiling on splitting, splitting only happens under damage, and every value of it builds the identical two heads at spawn. Four values, four identical photographs - a time-domain knob wearing the costume of a shape knob, and the exact finished-looking-experiment-that-answers-nothing this loop is supposed to refuse. start_depth is the same quantity made PRESENT: the crown is pre-grown by replaying the cut itself (SPLIT_RATIO 0.6, SPLIT_SPREAD 0.4, shared as constants with _on_damaged so the two paths cannot drift), giving 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 heads at 0.15 / 0.09 / 0.054 / 0.032 radius. Only the surviving generation is instantiated - the intermediate parents die the instant they split, and building them would leave hidden meshes inflating the capture AABB. The Label3D reads HEADS: n, DEPTH: d, so the frame carries its own caption.
dna.fixture_note: this is a CharacterBody3D that patrols from wherever it is dropped, at 1.2 m/s, from its first physics frame. Left alone it walks out of a fixed camera during the settle and the axis is measured against a moving subject. patrol_speed 0 parks it (velocity goes to zero, the leg animation stops) and detection_radius 0 keeps it out of DETECT/CHASE. Both are base-class exports defaulting to the shipped values, so they are fixture knobs and not axes.
dna.measurement_risk: 16 heads at depth 3 overlap: the split spread of 0.4 rad applied twice brings sibling branches back onto the same angle, so the visible count is lower than the head count. That is faithful - the live hydra does the same after two cuts - but do not read a smaller-than-expected difference between depth 2 and depth 3 as a dead axis. Check subject % and the label text before believing any faint verdict.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: nothing yet. `depth` is a common word in the fractals sequence but no sibling declares it as an axis, and start_depth means something narrower than depth-of-recursion: cuts already suffered. Taking a borrowed word here would have been a false claim of comparability.

fractal_hydra.description: Central body with branching heads on cylinder necks. Damage splits a head into two half-size copies — fractal branching up to depth 3. More heads means more attacks but less damage each. Cut one head, two grow back.
fractal_hydra.name: Fractal Hydra
fractal_hydra.qfep_connection: Punishment is its growth function: strike a head and two return at half scale, the pattern re-instancing itself down to depth three. Self-similarity as defense means your attacks are its recursion calls.

goomba_box.description: Folding cardboard box that patrols corridors. Stomp from above to flatten it — topology as vulnerability. Side contact deals damage.
goomba_box.name: Goomba Box
goomba_box.qfep_connection: Six faces, one weakness: the lid. The state machine grants it anger — DETECT, CHARGE — but its topology sealed its fate in advance; power sits unevenly on a body's surfaces, and the player learns to read bodies for their unguarded plane.

dna.default: stencil=ring, evidence=longhand - ring runs the same formula the mesh builder used to inline, over the same sample_count of 6, so _offsets[i] is the position the sphere was already given, and ring is also the only value that still ORBITS in _process_visual, which is the shipped animation untouched. evidence=longhand shows the body, the legs, the probes, the gradient arrow and the loss/lr label - everything _build_mesh has just created, visible - and adds no geometry, so _apply_evidence is a pure no-op on that rung. All three placements (Chamber_ML, Hazards_Zoo_6, and the curation_station collection in Curation_Bay_hazards_10) are bare tokens with no config, and apply_grid_config only assigns when the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already held, so nothing is rebuilt for them.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Eleven exports existed and every one was a quantity or a dimension: a learning rate, a radius, two annealing numbers, and five sizes of body part. The decision that carries the argument - WHICH POINTS THE ESTIMATE IS TAKEN FROM - was the same `angle = i/sample_count * TAU` formula written out longhand in three separate places (the mesh builder, the orbit animation and _compute_gradient), and the class had no apply_grid_config of its own, so the base forwarded health and speed and a map token could reach nothing else.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. This creature's own critical_parameter is `_sample_positions / _gradient_dir - 6-point gradient estimate determines movement`, and the six points on a horizontal circle were never a fact about gradient descent. A gradient is never measured, only INFERRED from a finite set of probes, and the choice of probes is the whole of what the optimiser can know: pair is one central difference and can only see along a line; axial is the textbook coordinate-wise partials and nothing between them; shell is twelve icosahedron vertices and the only value that admits the Y this creature has always had and thrown away in _process_chase; swarm is nine golden-angle points at mixed radii, not a stencil at all but a population. All deterministic - no randf anywhere in the resolution - so five variants are five pictures of one creature rather than five creatures. sample_count stays exported and undeclared: it is a count on the ring and a derived fact everywhere else, and four counts of the same circle is a picture of the same estimator four times.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: gradient_descent_visualization, promoted the same day - `evidence` with these four rungs, character for character, and behind it the wider motion family (koch_curve, box_counting_dimension, three_body_problem). Same question, and here it is asked of a PREDATOR rather than a diagram: the loss function is the space between it and you. `stencil` is deliberately a NEW word and shares nothing. The nearest neighbours would have been `basin` from the same artifact, which is a property of the landscape rather than of the sampler, and `frame` from basis_vectors_rig / xyz_coordinates, which is about which directions are agreed rather than which are probed. Borrowing either would have claimed a comparability that does not exist.
dna.fixture_note: this is a CharacterBody3D that starts in PATROL and walks its corners from the first physics frame, and the sweep now uses ONE camera for the whole run, so an unpinned creature drifts inside a fixed frame and the diff measures displacement instead of the axis. detection_radius 0 keeps it out of DETECT/CHASE with no player in the scene. patrol_speed 0 only bites because _on_ready's write of 1.2 was changed to fire only when the property still holds HazardCreatureBase's 1.8 - an unguarded write there discards anything set before add_child, which is exactly how the sweep applies values. Both are base-class exports at their shipped values in every real room, so they are fixture knobs and not axes.
dna.measurement_risk: trace -> longhand is the weakest step on the evidence axis and may read faint. With no player in the world _gradient_dir stays ZERO, so the arrow keeps its build position at the body centre and never orients, and the label reads loss=0.00, lr=3.0 - that rung is carried by a small cylinder and a line of text. result -> trace (the probes appear) and longhand -> axiom (spokes and chords, and the label switches to the update rule) are the steps that move pixels. Do not read a faint trace/longhand pair as a dead axis without looking at those two.
dna.still_note: every rung of both axes is standing geometry. The probes orbit under stencil=ring only, and that orbit is the shipped animation phase-locked to _state_time, which is identical across variants because each is instantiated fresh and captured after the same settle. Nothing else here is time-domain.

gradient_hunter.description: Sleek predator with orbiting sample-point particles. Gradient descent pathfinding toward player — gets stuck in local minima, anneals out with random teleport. Machine learning as locomotion strategy.
gradient_hunter.name: Gradient Hunter
gradient_hunter.qfep_connection: The loss function is you: six samples estimate the gradient of distance-to-player and it descends. Walls make local minima, so it does what optimizers do — waits three seconds, then teleports, and calls its desperation annealing.

grammar_markov.description: Tetrahedron with 4 colored state-faces. Markov chain transition matrix determines attack patterns — visible transition probabilities. Matrix mutates over time. Stochastic grammar made combative.
grammar_markov.name: Grammar Markov
grammar_markov.qfep_connection: Its behavior is legible exactly once: watch long enough and the transition matrix becomes learnable — then, every three cycles, the probabilities mutate. A stochastic grammar that punishes the statistics it invites you to gather.

graph_weaver.description: Network of 8 sphere-nodes connected by cylinder-edges. Reconfigures edges to create shortest path toward player with visible BFS/DFS traversal. Can cast edges as projectile attacks.
graph_weaver.name: Graph Weaver
graph_weaver.qfep_connection: Connectivity is the whole predator: it rewires its spanning tree into a shortest path aimed at you, walks a BFS wave along it, and can spend edges as projectiles. The attack surface is literally the adjacency list.

gridagent.description: Grid-traversing hazard agent spawned from map tokens like `gridagent:copy`.
gridagent.name: Grid Agent
gridagent.qfep_connection: A creature that walks the array — traversing the grid cell by cell, copying and patterning as it steps. The array given an inhabitant: where the other exhibits show the structure, this one shows what it is like to MOVE through indexed space, a body reading the lattice one address at a time.

hazards_demo.description: Test arena for all hazard creatures. Spawns plasma critters, stick tools, dormant egg-plant octapods, and an active crawler in a dark atmospheric arena with moody lighting and fog.
hazards_demo.name: Hazards Demo
hazards_demo.qfep_connection: The test arena where the danger fauna are let out together — plasma critters, crawlers, dormant egg-plants. Chance with consequences: the room where randomness stops being a visual and starts costing something.

helix_cylinder.description: Vertices on a helix form triangles into a closed faceted cylinder. Pineapple diamond topology. Flat triangle grid unfurls into a twisted tube. Kresling-inspired.
helix_cylinder.name: Helix Cylinder
helix_cylinder.qfep_connection: A flat triangle grid closes into a twisted faceted tube by lerping each vertex onto a helix; the pineapple's diamond lattice appears the moment the sheet's edges are identified. The cylinder was a quotient of the plane all along.

helix_cylinder_creature.description: Runtime fold creature — flat triangle grid folds into twisted faceted cylinder. Pineapple topology. Same vertices, same faces, only positions change. Driven by fold_amount.
helix_cylinder_creature.name: Helix Cylinder Creature
helix_cylinder_creature.qfep_connection: A cylinder is a flat grid that has agreed to identify its edges; here the agreement is continuous, fold_amount sliding the same triangles between page and tube. Aliveness is located in the twist — the shear that mere rolling-up would never add.

helix_fold.description: A triangle strip coils from flat zigzag ribbon into a helix via sin/cos. Five stages showing the fold progression. DNA springs spiral shells.
helix_fold.name: Helix Fold
helix_fold.qfep_connection: A zigzag ribbon coils into a spring with nothing but sin and cos per vertex, five stages standing side by side like specimens. The DNA iconography is earned honestly: a helix is what a strip does when both of its coordinates start rotating.

hull_crusher.description: Morphing convex polyhedron with orbiting point-nodes. Fires points as projectiles — each launch shrinks the convex hull. Points respawn over time. Teaches computational geometry through combat.
hull_crusher.name: Hull Crusher
hull_crusher.qfep_connection: Every attack is a vertex spent, and the hull — its body — shrinks to the extent of what remains. A geometry that pays for aggression out of its own definition, until respawn timers quietly restore the fiction of an inexhaustible form.

index_sentinel.description: A walking 4x4 grid that fires cells by [i][j] index, teaching array traversal through attack patterns. Row-major order, visual telegraphing of the next index.
index_sentinel.name: Index Sentinel
index_sentinel.qfep_connection: [i][j] with a muzzle: cells telegraph before firing in strict row-major order, so surviving means having internalized the traversal. Indexing stops being notation the first time it aims at you.

inflate_flock.description: Icosphere inflates from a point using vertex flocking — pressure pushes out, separation prevents overlap, cohesion holds shape. Organic breathing inflation. Same vertices, same faces.
inflate_flock.name: Inflate Flock
inflate_flock.qfep_connection: Inflation without a balloon equation: each vertex is a boid feeling outward pressure, separation from neighbors, cohesion toward the group, and the sphere emerges as their negotiated settlement. The surface breathes because no vertex is in charge.

isosurface_trap.description: Blobby metaball surface from point charges. Scalar field bulges toward player; contact equals damage proportional to field strength. The implicit surface made dangerous.
isosurface_trap.name: Isosurface Trap
isosurface_trap.qfep_connection: There is no wall, only a sum of charge-over-distance and a threshold: you are inside when the equation says so, and damage scales with the field's value at your body. The charges drift toward you — the boundary you are trying to read is also reading you.

joint_articulator.description: Central body with 6 limbs, each using a different joint type — hinge, ball, slider, revolute, prismatic, fixed. Each limb moves per its constraint. Joint physics made visible.
joint_articulator.name: Joint Articulator
joint_articulator.qfep_connection: Six limbs, six constraint vocabularies — hinge, ball, slider, revolute, prismatic, fixed — one body forced to speak them all at once. A taxonomy walking: each joint's freedom is exactly what the others are forbidden.

kaleidocycle_enemy.description: Tumbling ring of tetrahedra with 4 attack modes. Rolls toward player while continuously rotating through itself. Each face color triggers different attack: Fire (red), Ice (blue), Spike (purple), Shield (gold).
kaleidocycle_enemy.name: Kaleidocycle
kaleidocycle_enemy.qfep_connection: A closed kinematic chain where every attack face is always present, only rotated out of view: fire, ice, spike, and shield are one body's phases, not four weapons. When the shield face lands, invincibility arrives by pure topology of turn.

dna.default: posture=cycle, warning=none - cycle is the sentinel branch of _pin_twist(), which returns -1.0 and writes nothing at all, so the state machine keeps sole ownership of _twist and the shipped start pose (AIM at _twist 0.1) is untouched; warning=none is the `_:` arm of _build_warning() and adds no child. Neither key is named by any of the 7 existing placements, and configure() takes a word only when it validates AND differs, so a typo or a repeat leaves the fold and the dressing exactly where they were. Chamber_Forces, Corridor_Random_Game, ForcesArena, ForcesFoundations, ForcesSystems, Hazards_Zoo, Random_Game, TemplateMap_Descent13 and VectorApplied are byte-identical.
dna.was: declared nothing. Both axes were already written into kresling_spire.gd - warning on the hazard family pass, posture on 2026-08-03 - and the registry had never been told, so the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS while two working axes sat in the file. Derived from the source, not transcribed: WARNING_VALUES and POSTURES are the code's own constant lists.
dna.note: posture is WHICH OF ITS TWO BODIES the spire is wearing. The word is [[armadillo_eggling]]'s and the question is the same - a hazard that owns two bodies and a map that gets to say which one it stands in - but the values are deliberately NOT shared: a Kresling drum has no ball and no legs. _twist is the artifact's own declared critical_parameter, one DOF from 0 (tower) to 1 (disc), and the shipped spire never holds it still, which is precisely why a still cannot photograph the argument. cycle keeps the DISC-RISE-AIM-FIRE-COLLAPSE-RELOCATE schedule; disc pins the fold flat (a sniper firing off the floor says the rise was never the weapon); half holds the mid-fold a still would otherwise never catch; tower pins it extended, a permanent firing position. The pin is written AFTER the state machine each frame, so every combat number - fire_damage, fire_speed, shots_per_burst, fire_interval, optimal_range, detection_radius, disc_speed, max_health - is identical at all four values. warning is HOW MUCH THE HAZARD TELLS YOU BEFORE IT COSTS YOU ANYTHING, taken character for character from [[miura_crawler]], [[scissor_stalker]], [[kaleidocycle_enemy]] and [[path_block]]; the spire is the family's sniper case, the only member that never reaches you, so the only warning it could ever give is what it looks like from across the room. APPEARANCE ONLY - the builders add MeshInstance3D children, never a collider, never a group the combat code reads, never a distance.
dna.still_note: posture is the strong axis: disc is a hexagonal tile on the floor, tower is a mast, half is a twisted drum, and the silhouette differs at every value. warning is the same five-value scale the rest of the hazard family is measured on, sized from the exports rather than the live twist so the dressing never breathes with the fold.
dna.kin: warning shared with miura_crawler, scissor_stalker, kaleidocycle_enemy, path_block. posture shares the word with armadillo_eggling and nothing else.

kresling_spire.description: Kresling origami sniper tower - twisting cylinder that extends from compact disc to tall tower. Rolls as disc to reposition, rises by untwisting to snipe from elevation, collapses rapidly to relocate.
kresling_spire.name: Kresling Spire
kresling_spire.qfep_connection: In the Kresling fold rotation and translation are one motion: to rise and snipe it must untwist, to flee it must twist flat. It also enforces a standoff, backing away as you close, so the fight happens at the tower's chosen range, not yours.

dna.default: rule=life - life is [[3], [2, 3]], which is B3/S23, which is the `neighbors == 2 or neighbors == 3` that _step_ca wrote out by hand. The 1 existing placement passes no rule key, ca_seed defaults to 0 (the shipped unseeded randf soup, so every spawn still gets its own armour) and warmup defaults to 0 (all 36 cells sit on the alive material until the first tick half a second in, exactly as before). apply_grid_config regrows only when a value both validates and differs, so that room is unchanged.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The exports were ca_rows, ca_cols, two tick rates, a cell size and four colours: dimensions and decoration. The transition rule, the one decision that decides what the armour looks like, was written out longhand inside _step_ca, and the base class's apply_grid_config only forwarded health and speed, so a map token could not reach it.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. The @identity names the critical parameter as _grid state / _generation and _init_grid seeds at density 0.5 - and density is the wrong knob for the same reason complexity_pattern refused it hours earlier: under Life every starting density converges to the same sparse litter of still lifes, so five densities photograph as five indistinguishable torsos. What a still of this creature actually shows is HOW MUCH OF THE BODY IS ARMOURED, and that fraction is a property of the rule table, not of the soup - life and highlife decay to a few blocks, seeds sprays and empties, replicator fills to a periodic parity texture, maze and coral freeze into standing structure across most of the plate. The creature stops asserting Conway and starts showing what a different law would have armoured it with. Armour is also mechanical here, not only visual: _on_damaged reduces incoming damage by alive_count / 36, so the rule is simultaneously the defence budget.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: complexity_pattern - `rule` with these six values, and the RULES table itself, are copied from it character for character. That artifact is this automaton as a flat field; this one wears it on a torso. Same question, same words, and the two SHOULD measure alike, which is the check on whether the borrowing was honest. Deliberately not a new word: inventing one would have hidden a real comparison.
dna.fixture_note: four separate reasons, all defaulting to shipped behaviour so none of them is an axis. ca_seed pins the soup, without which six rule variants are six different random torsos and the sweep measures the RNG. warmup runs 10 generations at build time, without which every variant photographs the same undifferentiated 50% soup - at generation 0 no rule has spoken. 10 and not complexity_pattern's 80 because this board is 6x6 and bounded: life empties it within a few dozen generations and _step_ca then reseeds, which would hand the still a fresh random soup and undo the point. The two tick rates park the automaton after warmup so the frame is exactly generation 10 and not whatever the settle timing lands on. patrol_speed and detection_radius park the creature itself, which otherwise walks out of a fixed camera at 1.8 m/s.
dna.measurement_risk: the axis lives in a 0.4 x 0.4 plate on a creature about 0.95 m tall, so a fit-by-diagonal camera gives the grid roughly a third of the frame height. Emissive green against near-black dead cells is high contrast, which should carry it, but if the critic reports faint check subject % and add a framing hint below 1.0 rather than re-cutting the axis.

lifeform_walker.description: Walking creature with a 6x6 Game of Life grid on its torso. Living cells provide armor; Conway's rules run each tick. Dead automaton reinitializes. The cellular automaton made corporeal.
lifeform_walker.name: Lifeform Walker
lifeform_walker.qfep_connection: Its armor is not chosen, it is computed: Conway's rules tick across the torso and whichever cells happen to live are the plates that hold. Defense delegated to emergence — the creature hardens or opens depending on what a 6x6 automaton decides to become.

loving_triangle.description: A triangle-shaped companion that dances with the Becoming Catalyst. Triangles are the atom of all 3D worlds — every mesh reduces to triangles. This entity makes that visible. Not an enemy — a relational partner. It responds to each catalyst mode with its own transformation: folding, tiling, compressing, expanding. Evolves through tiers as lab sequences complete.
loving_triangle.name: Loving Triangle
loving_triangle.qfep_connection: The triangle embodies relational identity: the self constituted through encounter. Same potential (catalyst projectile), different relational context (triangle vs wall vs enemy), different manifestation. The simplest polygon that creates enclosure — the other that completes the becoming.

maze_spinner.description: Crystalline core that procedurally generates rotating maze walls. DFS-based maze generation with new random seed every 8 seconds. Navigate the gaps or take wall damage. The algorithm IS the enemy.
maze_spinner.name: Maze Spinner
maze_spinner.qfep_connection: DFS carves a perfect maze, then the seed rerolls every eight seconds and it carves another — memorization, the classic labor of maze-solving, is structurally worthless here. The corridor is rented, never owned, and it rotates while you rent it.

mesh_morpher.description: Shape-shifting creature morphing between sphere, cube, torus, and cylinder. Each topology has a different attack pattern — roll, slam, spin, sweep. Mesh topology as combat strategy.
mesh_morpher.name: Mesh Morpher
mesh_morpher.qfep_connection: Sphere rolls, cube slams, torus spins, cylinder sweeps — each attack is what that genus affords and nothing else. Identity-as-topology made hostile: to survive it you must read shape as constraint, not costume.

miura_crawler.description: Miura-ori folding enemy - flat corrugated sheet that crawls like an inchworm. Lies flat and nearly invisible, pops up when player approaches, uses zigzag locomotion. Can squeeze through gaps when flattened.
miura_crawler.name: Miura Crawler
miura_crawler.qfep_connection: One degree of freedom is a whole animal: cycling the fold amount corrugates a flat sheet into inchworm locomotion, and flatness doubles as camouflage. The threat is legible only when the geometry commits.

noise_field.description: 10x10 grid of height-varying tiles driven by Perlin noise. High tiles are danger zones, low tiles are safe. Noise scrolls continuously — the landscape of randomness shifts under your feet.
noise_field.name: Noise Field
noise_field.qfep_connection: Perlin's trick — randomness with spatial correlation — is what makes the danger legible at all: high red tiles announce themselves through their smooth neighborhoods. The field scrolls, so safety is a gradient you surf, not a place you reach.

dna.default: guise=pod - pod returns the shipped literals of _build_egg_plant() value for value: albedo (0.28, 0.35, 0.22), roughness 0.8, emission on, egg scale (1.0, 1.3, 1.0), five sepals tilted -0.3, six warts. The 1 existing placement gets the same dormant egg-plant, and only guise=bare touches the state machine (there is no shell to wait inside)
dna.was: twenty-eight exports, all of them rates, radii and durations - leap_speed, detect_pause, stun_duration, hatch_time. None of that survives a still photograph. The decision the header comment names as the whole point (is it a plant? an egg? food? danger?) was hard-coded inside _build_egg_plant()
dna.reads: guise is the category the creature presents BEFORE the relationship resolves it. pod is organic growth, stone is scenery, fruit is an invitation, husk is a thing that has already hatched so there is nothing left to fear, and bare refuses mimicry outright - the eight-legged animal standing in the open from the first frame. The hazard is identical in all five; only the claim about what it is changes
dna.fixture_note: the six warts scatter from a randomize()d RNG, so two renders of the same guise differ. pod_seed pins the scatter for the gallery only; the default 0 hands back the shipped RNG untouched
dna.declined: leg_count and gait. leg_count is a real export and visible in world space, but the legs are hidden for as long as the default guise is intact, so a leg axis swept against the default fixture returns four identical photographs of an egg; the 8 legs also come from a fixed octapod_ik.tscn rig, so the export only indexes into it. Gait is time-domain and invisible to a still by construction
dna.vocabulary_note: catalyst_foe.body declares octapod among curriculum|cube|mote|serpent|octapod|grand, but that axis is one cube choosing which silhouette to wear - octapod_crawler is the referent of that value, not a member of the family. An axis called body here would mean this creature's own morphology, a different question, so the word is not reused

octapod_crawler.description: Procedural 8-legged wall-crawling creature. Headcrab meets octopus. Patrols surfaces, detects player, chases and leaps. Can be stunned with fire. Future: befriend in lab, evolves through game.
octapod_crawler.name: Octapod Crawler
octapod_crawler.qfep_connection: It enters the world as a category error — pod, plant, egg, food? — and stays undecidable until the player's approach resolves it into enemy. Hostility here is not a property but a reaction: the crawler is dangerous because it was surprised.

octapod_ik.description: Eight-legged IK walker variant. Pure inverse kinematics locomotion without CharacterBody3D physics — legs find surfaces procedurally. The mathematical octapod.
octapod_ik.name: Octapod IK
octapod_ik.qfep_connection: Not a creature but the contract its whole family signs: eight skeleton chains, each FABRIK-bent toward a marker a SpringArm presses against the ground. The one-to-eight leg critters are subsets of this rig — a body plan kept as a reusable scene file, ancestry as infrastructure.

one_leg.description: Single IK leg demo — the fundamental unit of procedural locomotion. One joint chain finding ground contact. The building block from which all multi-legged creatures emerge.
one_leg.name: One Leg
one_leg.qfep_connection: The progression's axiom: one skeleton chain, one spring-found contact point, and a body that must bounce because balance on a single foot can only ever be serial. Everything the later critters elaborate — plant, stretch, step — is reduced here to whether the leg can reach the floor at all.

origami_bird.description: Origami crane that progresses through four fold stages: egg seed (0.0) → standing crane (0.4) → walking with alternating gait (0.6) → full wingspan flight (1.0). Twelve segments, paper-white materials, spring-damped fold dynamics. One fold_amount variable drives the entire lifecycle.
origami_bird.name: Origami Bird
origami_bird.qfep_connection: Twelve segments and a single scalar carry a crane from egg through standing and a sinusoidal walking gait to full wingspan — locomotion modes are just bands on the fold_amount axis. A lifecycle compressed to one dimension, with spring dynamics deciding how fast the paper is allowed to live.

origami_droideka.description: Magic-ball inspired fold shell using accordion pleats and braided ring bands; rolls compressed and deploys to fire.
origami_droideka.name: Origami Droideka
origami_droideka.qfep_connection: The same pleated shell is wheel, turret, and shield depending on where the fold sits; inflation_fire_bias decides how much firing exposes the core. Constraint doing the work of transformation — the sheet never changes, only its commitment.

origami_pyre_plane.description: A folded-paper rectangle of fire that sits beneath transport cubes. Its creased surface cycles through affine transformations — scale pulses, rotation sweeps, positional drift — while the rectangular shape remains invariant. Demonstrates that identity persists under transformation. Lethal on contact.
origami_pyre_plane.name: Pyre Plane
origami_pyre_plane.qfep_connection: It cycles scale, rotation, translation — exactly the transformations that preserve its rectangle — while the creases smolder orange; the invariant is the shape, the hazard is the heat. An affine-identity lesson taught by a floor that kills you for standing on the proof.

dna.default: census=pair, claim=placard - PRESERVES every existing placement exactly. There are three reach-paths, not the one the runner counted: a bare token in Hazards_Zoo_6, a curation_station collection in Curation_Bay_hazards_17 (whose #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags are the station's, not this creature's), and `proximity_spawner#type:paradox_stalker` in Chamber_Foundations, where ProximitySpawner.configure forwards only type / spawn_radius / despawn_radius / respawn_delay and the spawned creature therefore takes the script defaults. census=pair is special-cased in _ghost_offsets to return the two literal vectors _build_mesh used to write inline, (+sep/2, 0, 0) and (-sep/2, 0, 0), rather than the ring formula evaluated at n=2, because sin(PI) is 1.2e-16 and the shipped placement is entitled to a clean zero; _chase_offset does the same for the chase targets, returning dir*r and -dir*r. claim=placard makes _create_materials emit exactly the two lines it used to hold - ghost_a_color with real_emission, ghost_b_color with BLACK, each at its own alpha - and _build_claim_marks builds the one Label3D with the same text, font_size 22, pixel_size 0.002, modulate and position (0, 1.0, 0.05). _refresh_claim reproduces the old swap block byte for byte at n=2: emission on the holder, 0.7/0.3 alpha, `REAL: A`/`REAL: B` on the billboard. _on_damaged's `randf() > 0.5` became `randf() > 1.0 / n`, which at n=2 is the same number. The one placement is a bare token with no config, and apply_grid_config only assigns when the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already held, so nothing is rebuilt for it.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Eight exports existed: swap_interval, zeno_chance, lunge_speed, lunge_duration are all RATES or DURATIONS and invisible to a still; ghost_separation is a distance; the three Colors are palette. The class had no apply_grid_config of its own, so the base forwarded health and speed and a map token could reach nothing else. Two ghosts was written into _build_mesh three times over - two Node3Ds, two materials, two offsets - and never named.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. The swap itself is the headline behaviour and it is time-domain: a still cannot photograph an alternation, so swap_interval was NOT promoted - an axis over it would have produced identical tiles and a confident verdict about the capture rather than the design. What a still CAN see is how many bodies are standing there and whether anything in the frame says which is real, and between them those two are the whole paradox. `census` runs one (nothing to alternate between, so no contradiction, and _on_damaged's 1/n coin resolves to `you always hit it`) - pair (the liar's minimum, shipped) - triad (a majority exists, so the contradiction becomes a VOTE, which is how formal systems usually escape one) - chorus (five: the question `which is real` has become a question about a crowd, which is not the same question). `claim` runs placard (glow + dim + billboard, the contradiction fully captioned, shipped) - glow (visible, unnamed) - none (identical bodies, no emission, no text: the liar taken at its word and photographically unresolvable) - all (every body lit and every placard reading REAL: the contradiction asserted out loud by everyone at once). The ring is a cosine, not a randf, so N variants are N photographs of one creature.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: nothing, deliberately, on either axis. `claim` is NOT the furniture family's `tell` (mark|none|ghost|exemplar, on balance_puzzle / chair_assembly_puzzle and four siblings): that word asks how a puzzle reveals its SOLUTION, and this artifact has no solution state - the answer it would reveal changes every three seconds. Reusing the word would have put a creature with no target state in a family of puzzles that all have one, and the siblings would not have measured alike. `census` is a new word too; the nearest neighbour is the hazards family's `warning` (none|stain|cage|beacon|shroud), which is about telegraphing danger to the player and is a different question from how many claimants a self-referring thing fields. `census` does appear as a VALUE in two `evidence` and `vacancy` ladders elsewhere in the corpus; as an axis NAME it is unused, and no ladder is being borrowed.
dna.fixture_note: a CharacterBody3D that starts in PATROL and walks its corners from the first physics frame; with one camera for the whole run an unpinned creature drifts inside a fixed frame and the diff measures displacement instead of the axis. Both are plain HazardCreatureBase exports and _on_ready here writes NEITHER (it only calls add_to_group), so no guard was needed - unlike qfep_calibrator, promoted the same day, whose _on_ready had to be guarded before its fixture could bite. detection_radius 0 also keeps the ghosts out of the CHASE branch of _process_visual, so the rest offsets stay where _build_mesh put them.
dna.measurement_risk: the humanoids are small - a 0.15 m torso, a 0.06 m head - against a merged AABB that is dominated by ghost_separation, so the SUBJECT PERCENTAGE is the number to check before believing any verdict here. On `census`, one->pair->triad->chorus changes the body count and the AABB width together, so the fitter will re-frame and the diff may understate; compare subject % across variants first. On `claim`, placard->glow is a single billboard disappearing and is the weakest step; glow->none is a colour change across every body (cyan becomes magenta) plus the emission going out, and placard->all is every body lighting plus N placards, and those two are the steps that move pixels. Do not read a faint placard/glow pair as a dead axis.
dna.still_note: everything both axes build is standing geometry, resolved in _create_materials and _build_mesh before the first physics frame. The swap fires at 3.0 s and the settle is shorter than that, so a capture photographs the build state: body 0 holds the claim in every variant. The lunge and the Zeno teleport need a player in the world and there is none on the bench.

paradox_stalker.description: Two overlapping ghost silhouettes that swap which is real every 3 seconds. 50% chance damage passes through the wrong ghost. Zeno's paradox: sometimes halves distance to player instead of closing it.
paradox_stalker.name: Paradox Stalker
paradox_stalker.qfep_connection: Only one silhouette is real at a time and the bit flips every three seconds; strike the other and the blow passes through nothing. Sometimes it Zeno-steps, halving the distance instead of closing it — a hunter quoting the argument against motion while moving.

particle_emitter_hazard.description: Nozzle firing lifecycle-colored spheres with manual particle pool. Cycles between cone, fountain, and spiral emission patterns. Birth-white to active-yellow to dying-red. The particle system as weapon.
particle_emitter_hazard.name: Particle Emitter
particle_emitter_hazard.qfep_connection: Every projectile wears its age, birth-white cooling to dying-red, so dodging means reading lifecycle rather than trajectory. And the pool of thirty makes finitude the mechanic — even a weapon is a population with a birth rate.

pattern_mine.description: Mines with SDF contour rings marking danger zones. Cross the zero-contour and they detonate. Different ring shapes, pulsing indicators, and respawning after cooldown. Signed distance as survival instinct.
pattern_mine.name: Pattern Mine
pattern_mine.qfep_connection: The minefield publishes its own danger function: the torus rings at 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 are literal contour lines of the signed distance that detonates at zero. Rare honesty in a hazard — the mathematics of your death is fully disclosed, and still the boundary gets crossed.

plasma_critter.description: Shapeshifting energy substance — a critter that takes form based on relational context. Raw form shocks on contact. Touch with a stick → fire torch. Touch water → healing aura. Touch crystal → power orb. Q-FEP: same potential, different restraint.
plasma_critter.name: Plasma Critter
plasma_critter.qfep_connection: Raw it shocks, on a stick it becomes torch, in water it heals — the substance never changes, only the mediator, stored in code as a Form enum switched by whatever touches it. Harm and care as relational outcomes of one energy: the dual-nature claim run at creature scale.

proximity_spawner.description: Spawns enemies when player enters radius. Respawns after enemy death. Configure with type, spawn_radius, despawn_radius, respawn_delay.
proximity_spawner.name: Proximity Spawner
proximity_spawner.qfep_connection: E_entropy: the vent that answers approach — it spawns when the player comes near, so population is a function of attention. Nothing exists in the room until presence calls it out; the spawner makes observation itself a physical cause.

dna.default: admits=all, readout=numeral - PRESERVES every existing placement exactly. There are three reach-paths, not the one the runner counted: a bare token in Hazards_Zoo_7, a curation_station collection in Curation_Bay_hazards_11 (whose #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags are the station's, not this creature's), and `proximity_spawner#type:qfep_calibrator` in Chamber_QFEP, where ProximitySpawner.configure forwards only type / spawn_radius / despawn_radius / respawn_delay and the spawned creature therefore takes the script defaults. admits=all makes _build_beams call the same three blocks _build_mesh used to write out longhand, in the same order (phi, then delta_e, then constraint), with the same cylinders, tips, rotations and offsets, so _mesh_root ends up with the identical child list. readout=numeral builds the same Label3D with the same text, font_size 32, pixel_size 0.003, modulate and position (0, 0.7, 0), and rungs 2 and 3 are skipped so no gauge and no lattice geometry is created at all; the two loops added to _process_visual walk arrays that stay empty. The one placement is a bare token with no config, and apply_grid_config only assigns when the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already held, so nothing is rebuilt for it.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Eleven exports existed and every one of them was a RATE, an AMPLITUDE or a DIMENSION: phi_frequency, delta_e_frequency, constraint_frequency, three amplitudes, beam_length, beam_radius, base_damage, base_detection, base_attack_range. Not one is legible in a still photograph, which is exactly why the sweep had nothing to turn. The class had no apply_grid_config of its own either, so the base forwarded health and speed and a map token could reach nothing else.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. The oscillation and the spin ARE this creature's headline behaviour and both are time-domain, so neither was promoted - a still cannot photograph a frequency, and an axis over phi_frequency would have produced identical tiles and a confident INERT verdict about the capture rather than the design. What IS in the frame is the three beams (0.6 m each on a 0.9 m body) and the placard. `admits` asks which terms of E(S) = f(phi, delta_e, constraint) the instrument puts in the world - not how big they are but how many dimensions it claims the landscape has, which is a different theory per value rather than a different size. `readout` is the ordered evidence ladder for what it commits to about the numbers it is reading; rung 3 draws the parameter space as a unit cube with the three origin edges coloured gold/cyan/magenta and a marker at this instant's point, which is the one artifact in the corpus with a literal parameter space to put there. Everything both axes build is standing geometry with no randf in it, so N variants are N photographs of one creature.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: `readout` is taken character for character from commons/primitives/line/line.gd and its twin commons/primitives/point/xyz_slider_plate.gd (none < numeral < gradation < lattice), including their fallback rule that an unrecognised word builds as numeral rather than none, so a typo cannot delete a placard from a live room. Same question, same monotone ladder, and the siblings should measure alike on the none->numeral step.
