NOT the noise family's readout (relief|plate|column), which is about how a scalar field is given a surface - this artifact has no field. `admits` is deliberately a NEW word and shares nothing: the nearest neighbours would have been `evidence` (result|trace|longhand|axiom), which asks what proof of a LAW is in frame, and `stencil` from gradient_hunter, which asks where an estimate is sampled from. Both are about the apparatus's method; this is about how many terms the theory has, and borrowing either would have claimed a comparability that does not exist.
dna.fixture_note: a CharacterBody3D that starts in PATROL and walks its corners from the first physics frame; with one camera for the whole run an unpinned creature drifts inside a fixed frame and the diff measures displacement instead of the axis. base_detection (NOT detection_radius) is the knob that bites, because _apply_parameter_effects rewrites detection_radius every frame as base_detection + _constraint * 5.0. patrol_speed 0 only bites because _on_ready's write of 1.5 was changed to fire only when the property still holds HazardCreatureBase's 1.8 - an unguarded write there discards anything set before add_child, which is exactly how the sweep applies values. Both are exports at their shipped values in the one real room, so they are fixture knobs and not axes.
dna.measurement_risk: on `readout`, none->numeral is a whole billboard appearing and will move pixels; numeral->gradation adds three 0.28 m tracks and is smaller; gradation->lattice adds a 0.3 m cube and is large again. On `admits`, all->phi / all->delta_e / all->constraint each delete two of three beams and all->none deletes all three, so every step is a big subtraction - if these read faint, suspect the framing (the merged AABB is dominated by the beams, so removing them shrinks the subject and the fitter may zoom in, making the remaining body fill more of the frame rather than less). Compare subject % across the variants before reading a verdict.
dna.still_note: everything both axes build is standing geometry. The body spin, the emission pulse, the beam-length scaling and the label's digits are all time-domain and all identical across variants, because each variant is instantiated fresh and captured after the same settle - they are shared background, not signal.

qfep_calibrator.description: Morphing dodecahedron with 3 parameter beams — phi (rotation speed), delta_e (damage), constraint (detection). Parameters oscillate, creating emergent behavior from their interaction. The QFEP laboratory's creature.
qfep_calibrator.name: QFEP Calibrator
qfep_calibrator.qfep_connection: Three sinusoids — phi, delta_e, constraint — never reference each other in the code, yet the creature's moods emerge from their beat frequencies. F_order stacked on F_order still yields E_flux: the coupling happens in the body, not in the equations.

recursion_spiral.description: Fibonacci spiral of shrinking sphere nodes spawned at golden-angle intervals. Each node is 0.618x parent size up to depth 5. Recursive cleanup on death. The golden ratio as creature architecture.
recursion_spiral.name: Recursion Spiral
recursion_spiral.qfep_connection: The same 137.5 degrees that packs sunflower seeds packs threat: each node spawns at the golden angle, 0.618 the size of its parent, damage thinning as 1/depth. Phyllotaxis without a plant — the optimum does not care whether it arranges seeds or ordnance.

resonance_chamber.description: Transparent box with standing wave bars at node positions. Damage at wave nodes, safe at anti-nodes; harmonic frequency shifts every 8 seconds. Sound physics as spatial puzzle.
resonance_chamber.name: Resonance Chamber
resonance_chamber.qfep_connection: The standing wave partitions the room into lethal nodes and safe anti-nodes, and every eight seconds a new harmonic redraws the partition. Safety here is not a place but a solution to cos(n·pi·x/L) — and n keeps changing.

scissor_stalker.description: Spider-like enemy with Hoberman scissor linkage legs. Legs extend 3x their compact length for dramatic reach. Stalks with partially extended legs, pounces by rapidly extending, slams down to attack.
scissor_stalker.name: Scissor Stalker
scissor_stalker.qfep_connection: Amplification as menace: one angular parameter runs through the Hoberman linkage and a small joint change becomes threefold reach. Even the walk is only phase-offset sines on the same bars — no animator, just geometry paid out.

shell_roller.description: Icosahedron creature that retracts into a kickable shell. Kick it to send it rolling — it bounces off walls and damages other enemies on contact.
shell_roller.name: Shell Roller
shell_roller.qfep_connection: Retracting for safety produces exactly the projectile form: the kick that protects the player weaponizes the creature against its own kin, and momentum conservation arrives with a body count. Defense and ammunition were the same shape all along.

six_leg_critter.description: Six-legged procedural walker. Insect-like alternating tripod gait — three legs always grounded. The most common arthropod configuration.
six_leg_critter.name: Six Leg Critter
six_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Six thresholds firing independently keep drifting toward the insect answer — three feet down, three swinging — because with legs at 60° that is simply what does not fall over. Four hundred million years of hexapod convergence restaged as the accident of a step rule.

spatial_voronoi.description: Ground plane divided into Voronoi cells by drifting seed points. Each cell has a different danger type — safe, damage, slow, heal. Seeds drift and types shuffle, remapping the partition. Spatial decomposition as territory.
spatial_voronoi.name: Spatial Voronoi
spatial_voronoi.qfep_connection: Territory is nothing but nearest-neighbor arithmetic: your cell is whichever drifting seed you are closest to, and its verdict — safe, damage, slow, heal — reshuffles on a six-second clock. Borders wander because centers do; the map is a consequence, never a commitment.

sphere_droideka.description: Armadillidiidae-style spherical droideka. Rolls as compact ball of overlapping shell plates, unfolds to tripod stance with shield dome and twin blasters. Star Wars droideka inspired.
sphere_droideka.name: Sphere Droideka
sphere_droideka.qfep_connection: The trade is written into the state machine: as a ball it is fast and unhittable, deployed it is armed, shielded, and rooted — mobility and firepower held as strict complements, never both at once. Minimum surface for maximum volume, then the geometry cashes its efficiency in as armor.

spring_hopper.description: Coil spring creature that bounces rhythmically. Land on top when compressed to get launched upward — Hooke's law as creature.
spring_hopper.name: Spring Hopper
spring_hopper.qfep_connection: F = -kx given eyes and a patrol route: compression is stored potential, and the player's trick is to arrive at maximum displacement, riding the hazard's own restoring force upward. Threat and elevator are one mechanism, distinguished only by timing.

spring_mass_bouncer.description: 3x3 grid of sphere mass-nodes connected by springs with Hooke's law physics. Deforms on contact; spring tension equals damage. Visible soft-body simulation as creature.
spring_mass_bouncer.name: Spring Mass Bouncer
spring_mass_bouncer.qfep_connection: Nine masses and F = -kx is the whole psychology: contact damage scales with the tension you provoke, so it hurts you exactly as much as you deform it. Softness here is not gentleness — it is stored energy waiting on a displacement.

stick_tool.description: A simple wooden stick the player can grab. Hold near a Plasma Critter to transform it into a torch. The mediator between player and plasma — the relational bridge.
stick_tool.name: Stick Tool
stick_tool.qfep_connection: By itself it does nothing — no damage, no state, just a tip that lets plasma change ontology from hazard to torch. Mediation is the whole mechanic: the grasped stick extends the arm, and the extended arm re-signs the treaty with fire.

dna.default: accord=school - school deposits NOTHING. It seeds the stream that _spawn_boid draws from and then hands control straight back to the shipped timer: boids released one every spawn_interval on a random outward heading, all three rules at the shipped weights (sep 2.0 / ali 1.0 / coh 1.0) and the shipped 3.0 m/s cap. _reset_rules is never called on that branch, so not one of the four numbers is even written. The 1 existing placement is a bare token with no config, and apply_grid_config returns early unless `accord` is present, is a word the artifact actually builds, and DIFFERS from the word already held - so the pre-existing boids and damage keys can never tear down a live swarm.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Fourteen exports existed and every one was a quantity or a colour: a count, four rates and radii, seven weights, three colours. The seven weights are the interesting part - separation_weight, alignment_weight and cohesion_weight were exported as three independent floats, which is a knob per rule and not an argument. Nothing named the COMBINATION, and the combination is the whole of what this artifact teaches. apply_grid_config forwarded two keys, boids and damage, and neither reached a rule.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. The three deposited values do not wait for a flock to emerge - each lays down the settled arrangement its rule holds, synchronously and seeded - and each carries a low speed cap so that arrangement STANDS across the capture window instead of decaying into the same drifting cloud as school. The cap is the mechanism by which a standing shape stands, not the thing declared; at the shipped 3.0 m/s every deposit would have travelled fifteen metres before the first shot and the four values would have been four photographs of one cloud. lattice is spaced 0.6 m, deliberately wider than separation_radius 0.5, so the rule is satisfied everywhere and the ranks hold with visible air between every mote.
dna.kin: accord is boid_manager's axis, reused character for character, and boids_aquarium's before that. Same word, same four rungs, same question - which of Reynolds' three rules the neighbourhood is actually obeying - differing only in scale: a 20 m box there, a 1 m tank in the aquarium, a 0.5 m hive here. The three should measure ALIKE, and the deposits here are the same four constructions (uniform cloud, solid ball with tangential velocities, thin +X sheet, regular grid) scaled to a hive. This artifact's own critical_parameter is literally `boid rules (separation, alignment, cohesion)` and its truth is `three rules, and the swarm organizes itself`, so the borrowed word is the one it was already using in prose.
dna.declined: A SECOND axis on the HIVE STRUCTURE - the 0.5 m box body and its six honeycomb accents ringed at TAU/6 - was considered and declined. The accents are the only other hard-coded arrangement in the file, but what they decide is what the source LOOKS like, not what the artifact argues; re-cutting them into a comb or a chimney would have been a size-and-shape axis dressed up as a genome, and a weak second axis is how a promotion earns a faint verdict that gets misread as a fact about the design. One axis that carries the whole claim is the honest result here.
dna.still_note: READ THIS BEFORE CALLING ANY RUNG INERT. The three deposited values are standing geometry and photograph cleanly. `school` is the rung to watch: it is the only value that still spawns on the shipped timer at the shipped 3.0 m/s cap, so how many boids exist and how far they have drifted depends on exactly when the shutter falls, and with no player in the scene there is no seeking to hold them in - the hive tether does not fire until 12 m. Its frame is therefore a wide sparse cloud with a small hive in it, and the capture AABB counts every boid, so the hive can end up a speck. That is the shipped artifact photographed honestly, not a broken rung. If school's subject percentage comes back tiny, reach for dna.framing rather than for the default's behaviour - the 1 existing placement must keep drifting exactly as it drifts today.
dna.hang_note: checked against the named headless hang class before anything was added. boid_flocking never yields headless; this artifact is not it and does not share its mechanism. swarm_hive has no GPU compute, no await, no call_deferred in the build path and no wait-for-convergence: _process is O(n^2) arithmetic over at most max_boids = 20 agents, and every deposit added here is a bounded for-loop over max_boids that RETURNS. Nothing in the promotion can stall a capture.
dna.reads: the .tscn root is the scripted node (Node3D carrying swarm_hive.gd, class_name SwarmHive) so the axis is reachable from a map token and from the sweep. Determinism comes from a per-instance RandomNumberGenerator seeded per accord value; the global RNG is never touched, because seed()/randomize() from inside an artifact reseeds the whole process and poisons every other artifact in the same run. The one pre-existing global draw, the launch heading in _spawn_boid, now comes from that same stream - the same uniform angle on the same circle, from a source two runs share, so school photographs the same cloud twice.

swarm_hive.description: Stationary hive spawning boid particles that follow separation/alignment/cohesion rules plus player-seeking. Emergent collective behavior from simple local rules. Destroy the hive to disperse the swarm.
swarm_hive.name: Swarm Hive
swarm_hive.qfep_connection: Separation, alignment, cohesion — plus a fourth rule the textbooks omit: seek the player. Emergence weaponized, with one honest admission built in — even distributed behavior gets spawned from somewhere, and the hive is where you end it.

techstrider.description: Tall mechanical strider with long articulated legs. Patrols elevated paths, steps over obstacles. A walking architecture — the legs ARE the structure.
techstrider.name: Tech Strider
techstrider.qfep_connection: The gait is pure ornament: hip and knee swing on a 120-degree phase-offset sine while the body translates by fiat, never once asking the ground. Walking architecture, yes — but the walk is a costume the movement wears.

tentacle_cube.description: A cube with procedural tentacles extending from its faces. Combines rigid geometry with fluid organic motion — the grid cell that grew limbs.
tentacle_cube.name: Tentacle Cube
tentacle_cube.qfep_connection: A grid cell in good standing until you close within four meters — then the cube confesses, unfolding the jointed tentacles it had folded into rigidity. Category here is not a kind but a state with hysteresis: deploy at 4 m, retract at 6.

tesseract_phaser.description: Wireframe hypercube with 16 vertices and 32 edges. 4D rotation phases parts in and out of hittability — vertex alpha based on W-depth. The fourth dimension as combat mechanic.
tesseract_phaser.name: Tesseract Phaser
tesseract_phaser.qfep_connection: Most of its body sits at W-depths you cannot reach; combat is the thin slice where its four dimensions intersect your three. What reads as phasing trickery is projection being honest — the creature was always whole, you were always partial.

three_leg_critter.description: Three-legged procedural walker. Tripod gait — the minimum legs for static stability. Always has a support triangle.
three_leg_critter.name: Three Leg Critter
three_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Three planted feet make the first polygon that does not negotiate with falling; a leg may lift only when its stretch passes a threshold, so stability is not a state but a budget spent one foot at a time.

two_leg_critter.description: Two-legged procedural walker. Bipedal gait emerges from alternating step cycles. The simplest creature that must solve balance.
two_leg_critter.name: Two Leg Critter
two_leg_critter.qfep_connection: With two contacts there is no support polygon, only a line — so the code plants, stretches, and catches, and every stride is a fall filed under 'step'. Balance is bookkeeping done fast enough to look like poise.

waterbomb_enemy.description: True rigid-foldable origami enemy using waterbomb tessellation. Faces remain rigid during folding; geometry is computed from kinematic constraints. Rolls collapsed, unfolds to flower shape when attacking.
waterbomb_enemy.name: Waterbomb Enemy
waterbomb_enemy.qfep_connection: The shell does not fake it: rigid waterbomb faces fold under real geometric constraint, so the rolling ball and the open flower are one crease pattern read at two dihedral angles. Proximity, not damage, turns the page — approach is what makes it bloom.

waterbomb_hopper.description: Bouncing waterbomb tessellation enemy. Origami-themed hazard with a waterbomb base shape built from triangular faces. Bounces sinusoidally with squash-and-stretch, fold angle oscillates for a breathing effect. Patrols a rectangular path, chases on detection.
waterbomb_hopper.name: Waterbomb Hopper
waterbomb_hopper.qfep_connection: Its sibling blooms in place; this one reads the same fold as a spring — compression stores the hop, squash-and-stretch replays the crease as rhythm while it patrols its rectangle. One tessellation, two ontologies: origami as structure there, as stored energy here.

wave_rider.description: Ribbon of 20 box segments in sine wave formation. Oscillation frequency ramps on detection; attacks at resonance with projectile bursts. Wave physics as creature locomotion.
wave_rider.name: Wave Rider
wave_rider.qfep_connection: Twenty segments sampling one sine — no segment is the creature, the phase relation is. Being detected ramps its frequency toward resonance, and at the peak the wave discharges: attention literally raises its energy state.

dna.default: body=curriculum, phase=curriculum - both are the sentinel meaning DO NOT SEED: the stage still comes from HazardManager/soft_stages.json and the personality still comes from the deferred curriculum query, so the 11 map cells naming this token render exactly what they rendered before the promotion
dna.was: the foe's body was whatever the spine position happened to make it, and every placement met it at the angry end of the arc — the two parameters existed as apply_grid_config string keys (critter_stage, initial_state) that no registry reader could see, so the sweep read the script, found no @export, and refused it as having no turnable knobs
dna.note: the catalyst system itself is untouched — no bracelet, no lease clock, no sequence binding. 'curriculum' and the first explicit value of each axis photograph alike in a probe with no HazardManager (the query falls back to order 0 / personality foe); that redundancy is the sentinel's meaning made visible, not a dud value. The cellular stage 'many' is deliberately not an axis value: it differs from octapod only in how many the VENT emits, which one still of one creature cannot show.

catalyst_foe.name: Catalyst Foe
catalyst_foe.description: Biome-borne grey-goo foe. Walks toward the player one cell every step_period_s. When the catalyst projectile hits it (any mode — uses hit_by_projectile contract), phase-shifts to FRIEND state, takes the projectile color, and walks toward the nearest remaining foe to convert it on contact. The unifying enemy of Ada Research: the angry are biome-borne, the catalyst doesn't kill, transformation propagates.

catalyst_vent.name: Catalyst Vent
catalyst_vent.description: Biome corruption seam that emits CatalystFoe bodies on a timer until wave_size is reached, then goes quiet. Tall translucent grey pillar so the spawn point is visible from any camera angle. VR mirror of the /editor e:RATE:WAVE utility token.

death_pylon.description: A pylon stand that breathes death in a cycle. During the charge it drinks energy from the ground - a wide field of grid-cells and energy motes is sucked up into its swelling, brightening core (a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D pulling everything inward through the glowing intake ring). At full charge it fires a jet of fire straight at the player and, within kill_range, kills them via the DeathEffect autoload. Then it dims, gathers again, and repeats. The lesson is conservation: it takes from the world a long time before it gives it all back at once. Particle technique adapted from the godot-xr-tools particle galleries (additive fire gradient, attractor suck).
death_pylon.name: Death Pylon

parameters.charge_time: seconds to fully charge before firing (default 4.2)
parameters.cooldown_time: seconds to recover before charging again (default 1.5)
parameters.kill_range: radius within which the discharge kills the player (default 9.0)
parameters.grid_n: NxN ground grid that gets sucked in (default 5)
parameters.preview: 0..1 - jump into the charge for a still capture
parameters.preview_fire: bool - force the discharge for a capture

edge_zone_crystal.name: Edge Zone — Crystal (order-death)
edge_zone_crystal.description: A zone frozen at pure order (lambda=0): a cold crystalline lattice that harms while it holds its dead-perfect shape. Stand in it to RETUNE it toward the living edge (lambda~0.4) — it goes green and quiet; walk away and it freezes again. The thesis-mechanic: the world tries to freeze, you keep it alive.
edge_zone_crystal.qfep_connection: Lambda decays toward zero — the F_order death, the completed lattice — unless a body stands in the ring and retunes it back to 0.4. Order left alone finishes itself, and finishing is fatal: damage ticks precisely when the zone is most resolved.

edge_zone_dissolve.name: Edge Zone — Dissolve (chaos-death)
edge_zone_dissolve.description: A zone boiling at pure chaos (lambda=1): formless magenta particles scattering, harming while nothing can hold. Stand in it to RETUNE it toward the living edge (lambda~0.4); leave and it dissolves again. The other of the two deaths — both fail the same way, and life is the edge held between them.
edge_zone_dissolve.qfep_connection: The mirror death: lambda drifts to one, pure E_flux, the zone boiling into particles that keep no form. The same living 0.4 must be held from the opposite side — proof that the edge is not a compromise between order and chaos but a position approached against either drift.
